The firsrt step is to read in the Crowd Counting Consortium data. I downloaded the three availible phases; 2017-2020, 2021-2024, and 2025's currently availiable data.
```{r}
#library(tidyverse)
#library(lubridate)
```
```{r}
ccc_files <- list.files("data/raw/ccc", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
ccc_files
```
I want to stack the three csv files into one table. 
```{r}
ccc_raw <- ccc_files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) |>
        rename_with(tolower)) |>
  list_rbind()

names(ccc_raw)
nrow

ccc_raw |>
  head()
```
I have run into a program where the three phases all call the "protest inciting issue" different column names. The older phases use "issues," whereas the newer phases use "issues_tags." 
```{r}
ccc_raw |>
  summarise(
    issues       = sum(!is.na(issues)),
    issue_tags   = sum(!is.na(issue_tags)),
    tags_summary = sum(!is.na(issue_tags_summary)),
    total_rows   = n()
  )

ccc_raw <- 
  ccc_raw |>
  mutate(topic = coalesce(issue_tags, issues, issue_tags_summary))

sum(is.na(ccc_raw$topic))

ccc_raw |> count(topic, sort = TRUE) |> head(20)
sum(is.na(ccc_raw$topic))

climate <- ccc_raw |>
  filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(topic), "environment|climate"))

nrow(climate)
climate |> count(topic, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)
```
```{r}
ccc_raw |>
  filter(is.na(topic)) |>
  mutate(year = str_sub(date, 1, 4)) |>
  count(year)
```
